governing_document.reason: 2026-18423 is a correction to AD 2026-17-03 that republishes the entire regulatory text. It changes paragraph (g) by restoring the omitted word "blade". As the latest correction that republishes the regulatory text, its text controls wherever it differs from final rule 2026-16954. All other paragraphs are identical to the final rule.

corrections.original_text: At the next engine shop visit after the effective date of this AD where the 3rd stage HPC rotor is exposed, replace the full set of 3rd stage HPC rotor blades with parts eligible for installation.
corrections.corrected_text: At the next engine shop visit after the effective date of this AD where the 3rd stage HPC rotor blade is exposed, replace the full set of 3rd stage HPC rotor blades with parts eligible for installation.

eligible_parts.description: A 3rd stage HPC rotor blade having P/N 6C8368, 6C8403, or later approved P/N. The definition is open-ended: any later approved P/N also qualifies.
A 3rd stage HPC rotor blade modified to P/N 6A8353-001 or P/N 6A8688-001.

required_actions.description: At the next engine shop visit after the effective date of this AD where the 3rd stage HPC rotor blade is exposed, replace the full set of 3rd stage HPC rotor blades with parts eligible for installation.
required_actions.condition_description: The 3rd stage HPC rotor blade is exposed at that engine shop visit.

ambiguities.description: Paragraph (g) conditions the action on a shop visit "where the 3rd stage HPC rotor blade is exposed." That phrase is not the term defined in (h)(2), "3rd stage HPC rotor blade exposure," which means removal of any 3rd stage HPC rotor blade from the HPC stage 3 to 8 drum. The text does not say whether the (h)(2) definition governs "is exposed" in (g). This determines which shop visits trigger the replacement.
readings: The (h)(2) definition applies: the replacement is due at the first engine shop visit, inducted after the effective date, at which any 3rd stage HPC rotor blade is removed from the HPC stage 3 to 8 drum.

"Exposed" carries its ordinary meaning, which is broader than removal from the drum (for example, the blades become accessible or visible when the HPC is opened). Under this reading the replacement could be due at a shop visit where no blade is removed from the drum.

notes: affected_parts is empty. No required action contains a list or table of specific parts. The P/Ns 6A8353 and 6A8688 appear only in the applicability paragraph (c), so they are recorded as the part condition.

Paragraph (g) requires replacing the full set of 3rd stage HPC rotor blades, not only the individual blades having P/N 6A8353 or 6A8688. applies_to is coded part_condition_parts because the action targets the 3rd stage HPC rotor blades named in the part condition. The proofreader should confirm that this coding captures the full-set scope.

No flight-cycle, calendar or other hard compliance limit is stated. The only compliance time is the conditional shop-visit trigger in (g). Paragraph (f) states "Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done."

An "engine shop visit" is defined in (h)(3) as the induction of an engine into the shop for maintenance. The final-rule preamble states it is not the FAA's intent to require engines inducted into a shop visit before the effective date to comply.

The proposed rule (2025-20088) used a different trigger: "At the next 3rd stage HPC rotor blade exposure after the effective date of this AD." The final rule changed (g) to a shop-visit trigger and added (h)(3) in response to a United Airlines comment. The (h)(2) definition was retained even though (g) no longer uses that exact term.

The final-rule preamble states that replacing the blades per IAE AG SB V2500-ENG-72-0716, dated October 4, 2024, demonstrates compliance. That SB is not referenced in the regulatory text. Paragraph (k) states no material is incorporated by reference.
The eligible-part definition in (h)(1)(i) includes "or later approved P/N". A screening program cannot resolve this from the listed P/Ns alone.
No paragraph of the AD prohibits installation of parts.
The only change made by correction 2026-18423 is in (g); the effective date remains September 24, 2026.
The final-rule preamble estimates 1,462 affected U.S.-registry engines; the NPRM estimated 1,496.
